public_sources.title: Safe testing
public_sources.relevance: Conditional e-variables can be constructed just in time from past information; their products remain safe under optional continuation when each next factor is conditionally e-valid.

public_sources.title: Online control of the familywise error rate
public_sources.relevance: Alpha-spending controls strong FWER over a potentially unbounded online stream; resetting a per-test level across recertifications is not lifetime control.

public_sources.title: Dynamic e-closure for online hypotheses with any-time-valid evidence
public_sources.relevance: Recent theory treats hypotheses that arrive online while evidence evolves over time and emphasizes globally summable weighting/coherence across an expanding hypothesis universe.

public_sources.title: Sequential (Quickest) Change Detection: Classical Results and New Directions
public_sources.relevance: Change monitors trade false alarms against post-change detection delay; a degradation monitor is inherently reactive and cannot certify that no unobserved change has just occurred.

public_sources.title: Batch Invariance - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official current example of a deterministic-by-construction serving mode with explicit supported-domain and performance limitations.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official warning that default serving is not reproducible and current reproducibility scope is tied to the same hardware and vLLM version.

public_sources.title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
public_sources.relevance: Primary systems evidence for decode-verify-rollback determinism, supporting a contract-certified path distinct from empirical mismatch certification.

public_sources.title: CoRun: Padding is Simple and Efficient for Deterministic LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Recent primary evidence that deterministic inference can recover substantial performance relative to batch-invariant approaches, while remaining system- and scope-specific.

main_result.title: Lifetime-valid multi-fingerprint admission/demotion needs a non-resetting risk ledger, and empirical admission alone cannot certify arbitrary future drift.

state_machine.transition: to CONTRACT_CERTIFIED if a deterministic contract explicitly covers the exact fingerprint/domain; otherwise to CALIBRATING with a fresh admission attempt

state_machine.rule: Allocate admission level a_j predictably from a global lifetime certification ledger before seeing this attempt's calibration outcomes. Run a one-sided Bernoulli mismatch e-process against the bad null p>=epsilon_max; fixed mixtures over p1<epsilon_max are allowed.
state_machine.transition: cross 1/a_j -> STAT_LEASED; failure/timeout -> UNCERTIFIED or QUARANTINED. The allocation is never reset or refunded in the baseline arbitrary-dependence design.

state_machine.rule: Hedging is permitted only under an explicit epoch-stability/conditional-mismatch assumption and a finite lease. Attach a degradation monitor and pin every evaluation to fingerprint_epoch_id, admission_attempt_id, epsilon bound, lease generation and risk allocation.
state_machine.transition: alarm, fingerprint/config mutation, lease expiry or invalidation -> QUARANTINED

state_machine.rule: Hedging may use the deterministic contract only inside its documented hardware/runtime/model/config domain. No empirical parent-average mismatch bound may expand that domain.
state_machine.transition: contract mismatch or scope drift -> QUARANTINED immediately

state_machine.rule: No fastest-selected stochastic output may enter new statistical evidence. In-flight audits fail closed to unresolved unless all used outputs remain independently justified under the frozen generation.
state_machine.transition: fresh/disjoint recertification evidence or restored deterministic contract -> new certification generation; never revive an old generation in place

lifetime_risk_ledger.certification: Let A_cert be the lifetime probability budget for falsely certifying a bad statistical fingerprint. For admission attempt j, choose predictable a_j>=0 with pathwise sum_j a_j<=A_cert. If each fresh admission e-value is conditionally valid for its bad null, union/iterated-expectation control gives P(any false statistical certification)<=A_cert without independence and without requiring fingerprint identities to be known in advance.
lifetime_risk_ledger.evaluation: Reserve a separate A_eval for false improvement commits conditional on every used fingerprint satisfying its frozen mismatch guarantee. Then P(any false commit attributable either to bad certification or evaluation noise)<=A_cert+A_eval. A deterministic-contract path replaces A_cert only inside the contract's actual domain; implementation/scope failure is an engineering assumption, not free statistical alpha.
lifetime_risk_ledger.demotion: False demotion is primarily an availability error, not a false-commit error. If lifetime control of unnecessary demotions is desired, maintain a separate non-resetting B_alarm ledger with predictable b_j and sum b_j<=B_alarm. Type-II miss probability/detection delay remains a separate metric.
lifetime_risk_ledger.recertification: Every recertification consumes a new admission allocation from the same lifetime ledger. Resetting the same alpha after each demotion is invalid lifetime accounting.

reset_counterexample.independent_illustration: If each recertification independently has false-admission probability 0.01 and the level is naively reset, the probability of at least one false admission is 9.56% after 10 attempts, 18.21% after 20, and 63.40% after 100. This is only an independence illustration; the non-resetting alpha-spending guarantee does not require independence.
reset_counterexample.baseline_schedule_example: A simple infinite-horizon fallback is a_j=A_cert/[j(j+1)], whose sum is A_cert. More powerful online-closure/fallback variants may recycle level under their additional assumptions, but the robust baseline is a pathwise summable ledger.

prospective_drift_impossibility.result: An empirical calibration pass plus a reactive degradation monitor does not, by itself, prove that the next production/evaluation request still has mismatch probability <=epsilon_max under unrestricted drift.
prospective_drift_impossibility.reason: A distribution can satisfy the calibration model up to time tau and change immediately after tau. Any monitor requires post-change observations to detect that event; quickest-change theory explicitly optimizes detection delay subject to false-alarm constraints rather than eliminating delay.
prospective_drift_impossibility.consequence: STAT_LEASED must carry an explicit stability/conditional-bound assumption or a separately budgeted drift-hazard assumption. If no such assumption is defensible, statistical certification cannot justify fastest stochastic hedging; use canonical attempts or deterministic-by-construction verification.
prospective_drift_impossibility.mid_audit_policy: On a degradation alarm or fingerprint invalidation, quarantine the entire active certification generation. Do not continue revealing fastest-selected outcomes under that generation. The conservative default is to mark the affected audit unresolved and restart with canonical/recertified evidence rather than splice pre- and post-alarm evidence.

admission_cost_stress.status: Worker-local Bernoulli Monte Carlo plus analytic thresholds; not measured serving-system mismatch rates.
interpretation: Lifetime alpha does not make late recertification impossible because e-process thresholds grow only logarithmically in 1/a_j, but statistical certification can still require thousands of stratum-specific conformance pairs at epsilon=.005.

For a rare stratum seen naturally in only 0.1% of traffic, collecting 2276 stratum observations would require about 2.276 million total requests in expectation under proportional sampling; deliberate probes reduce wall time but consume explicit compute.

A deterministic contract that genuinely covers many rare strata can replace this repeated per-stratum statistical sample burden, but only inside its documented domain and with its own performance/conformance cost.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Never reset certification or monitor error levels after recertification; keep lifetime ledgers keyed by immutable attempt/generation ids.

Separate three risks: false statistical certification, false improvement commit conditional on valid certification, and false degradation alarm. Summing or recycling them without a proof conflates different errors.
A degradation non-alarm is not evidence that no drift occurred. Report detection-delay sensitivity separately from false-alarm validity.
Statistical mismatch certification is a lease under explicit stability assumptions, not a timeless property of a fingerprint. Configuration mutation always creates a new generation.
If future conditional mismatch can drift adversarially with no bound, only canonical inference or deterministic-by-construction verification gives a clean prospective safety path.
On mid-audit invalidation, fail closed to unresolved and do not mix fastest-selected evidence across certification generations.
scope_guards: The admission e-process construction assumes a Bernoulli mismatch variable and a null stated in terms of the calibration process's conditional mismatch probabilities. Generalizing a calibration rejection to future requests requires an explicit stability/exchangeability/contract assumption.
The Monte Carlo uses a stationary true mismatch probability 0.001 and the stated fixed alternative mixture. It demonstrates sample-cost scale only.

The A_cert+A_eval union bound is intentionally conservative. Dynamic e-closure/online closure may improve power, but importing stronger procedures requires checking their dependence and conditional-validity assumptions.

Deterministic serving contracts are not universal: current vLLM documentation scopes reproducibility to supported modes/hardware/version, and recent deterministic systems report nontrivial system-specific tradeoffs.
A monitor can control false alarms under its null; it cannot guarantee zero post-change exposure before detection.

frontier.action: Derive a joint risk budget including a bounded drift-hazard term D_lease. Quantify when a finite statistical lease with A_cert+A_eval+D_lease is cheaper than canonical inference, and show the exact failure when D_lease is unbounded.

Optimize global admission alpha allocation and deliberate conformance probes across rare/common fingerprints under a fixed compute budget. Compare simple 1/[j(j+1)] spending with value-weighted predictable allocations and online-fallback/closure upgrades.

Construct a per-evaluation verification firewall that can preserve some hedging latency without a stationarity assumption: freeze attempt identity, verify canonical equivalence before statistical reveal, and measure the latency/occupancy cost against deterministic-by-construction inference.

Stress the state machine under abrupt within-fingerprint drift, repeated demotion/recertification and many adaptively created fingerprints. Track lifetime false certification, false commit, unnecessary demotion, detection delay and unresolved audit rate separately.

exact_next_action: Add an explicit lease-drift budget D_lease to the lifetime theorem and solve the three-way tradeoff among statistical lease certification, canonical single-attempt inference, and deterministic-contract/verified-execution paths for rare fingerprints. The key question is whether any practical bounded-drift assumption can make statistical hedging cheaper without hiding first-post-change exposure.
